Empirical Research Plan  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with a shift–share (Bartik-style) treatment intensity, complemented by an event-time panel-event-study.

Why DID?  
• The question is whether an exogenous funding shock to some prime funds (triggered by the June-2011 Euro-bank scare) spills over to unrelated U.S. borrowers.  
• The shock is plausibly exogenous to the fundamentals of U.S. non-Eurozone issuers; it varies only through the pre-existing network linking each issuer to funds that were more vs. less exposed to Euro-banks.  
• A DID exploits (i) cross-sectional heterogeneity in pre-shock exposure and (ii) the timing of the shock (pre vs. post June-2011).  
• The monthly Form N-MFP data give a balanced panel from March–August 2011, ideal for DID and for a finer grained event-study.

Formally, we estimate:

 Outcome_{i,t} = α_i + γ_t + β · (HighExposure_i × Post_t) + ε_{i,t}  

or, with continuous exposure,

 Outcome_{i,t} = α_i + γ_t + β · Exposure_i × Post_t + ε_{i,t}  

where Exposure_i is predetermined using March–May 2011 portfolios.

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
• Continuous: Exposure_i = ∑_f w_{if,pre} · EuroShare_f,pre  
 – w_{if,pre}: share of issuer i’s CP held by fund f in March–May 2011.  
 – EuroShare_f,pre: fund f’s fraction of assets in Euro-zone banks in March–May 2011.  
• Binary version for robustness: HighExposure_i = 1[Exposure_i above median].

Control group  
• Issuers in the lowest quartile (or below median) of Exposure_i serve as controls—they rely mainly on funds that were not hit by Euro-bank concerns.

Treatment timing / event date  
• Event date: 15 June 2011 (Moody’s downgrade review).  
• Post_t = 1 for June–August 2011; Pre_t = 0 for March–May 2011.  
• For the event-study we use monthly leads/lags from −3 to +3 months.

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of the shock, outcomes (commercial-paper volume, yields paid, rollover success, etc.) for high- and low-exposure issuers would have evolved in parallel.  
 Plausibility: Within a 3-month pre-period we can test for pre-trends; no news affecting only high-exposure issuers was released during March–May 2011.

A2. Shock exogeneity: Outflows from high-Euro funds were driven by concerns about Euro-zone banks, not by information about the treated U.S. issuers.  
 Plausibility: Issuers are non-European; the downgrade was unrelated to their fundamentals.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers across control firms).  
 Plausibility: Possible but must be discussed—re-allocation of funding could affect controls (see threats).

A4. No differential measurement error in Exposure_i.  
 Plausibility: Exposure is built from mandatory SEC filings; any error is classical and time-invariant (pre-determined).

================================================================  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
T1. Differential pre-trends or anticipation.  
 • Test for leads in the event-study.  
 • Include issuer-specific linear trends or flexible pre-period time effects.

T2. General market stress after June 2011 (e.g., U.S. debt-ceiling standoff).  
 • Add issuer-rating × time fixed effects.  
 • Control for VIX, Libor-OIS, aggregate CP outstanding.  
 • Triple-difference: compare prime-fund funded issuers to issuers relying on other investors (e.g., asset managers, banks).

T3. Re-allocation of funding (controls get more funding, violating SUTVA).  
 • Check whether low-exposure issuers’ total CP rises post-shock.  
 • Report results using alternative controls (e.g., non-MMF funded issuers).  
 • Interpret β as the average differential change—still policy-relevant.

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages ----------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE regressions
library(did)          # Goodman-Bacon decomposition (optional)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Data Loading -----------------------------------------------
fund   <- fread("fund_month.csv")      # one row per fund-issuer-month
issuer <- fread("issuer_month.csv")    # issuer-level outcomes

# 2. Construct pre-shock exposure --------------------------------
# restrict to March-May 2011 (pre-period)
pre_period <- fund[month %in% c("2011-03","2011-04","2011-05")]

# Euro share of each fund in the pre-period
euro_fund <- pre_period[, .(EuroShare_f = mean(fund_euro_share, na.rm=TRUE)),
                        by = fund_id]

# Fund weights within each issuer (share of issuer CP bought by fund)
w_if <- pre_period[, .(cp_amt = sum(cp_amount, na.rm=TRUE)),
                   by = .(issuer_id, fund_id)]
w_if[, w_if := cp_amt / sum(cp_amt), by = issuer_id]

# Shift–share exposure for each issuer
exposure <- merge(w_if, euro_fund, by="fund_id")
exposure <- exposure[, .(Exposure = sum(w_if * EuroShare_f)), by = issuer_id]

# High/Low dummy
exposure[, HighExposure := as.integer(Exposure > median(Exposure))]

# 3. Merge with issuer outcomes ---------------------------------
issuer <- merge(issuer, exposure, by="issuer_id")

# Post dummy
issuer[, Post := as.integer(month >= "2011-06" & month <= "2011-08")]

# 4. Main DID regression ----------------------------------------
# Example outcome: log CP outstanding
est <- feols(log(cp_outstanding) ~ Exposure:Post | issuer_id + month,
             data = issuer, cluster = ~issuer_id)
summary(est)

# 5. Event-study -------------------------------------------------
issuer[, rel_month := as.integer(as.yearmon(month) - as.yearmon("2011-06"))]
for (k in -3:3) issuer[, paste0("D",k) := as.integer(rel_month==k)]
leadlag <- paste0("Exposure*D", -3:3, collapse = " + ")

es <- feols(log(cp_outstanding) ~ issuer(Exposure) + Exposure*Post |
              issuer_id + month,
            data = issuer) # simplified; see Sun & Abraham for full ES

# 6. Robustness: use binary treatment ---------------------------
est_bin <- feols(log(cp_outstanding) ~ HighExposure:Post | issuer_id+month,
                 data=issuer, cluster=~issuer_id)
summary(est_bin)
```

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Theory: If relationships with prime funds are sticky and approval constraints bite, funds suffering outflows will cut positions across *all* of their incumbent issuers, not only Euro-banks. Issuers disproportionately connected to those funds should see:  
• Lower CP issuance volumes (−5 % to −10 % relative).  
• Slightly higher CP yields (+5–10 bp).  
• Increased reliance on backup bank lines / long-term debt.

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = satisfied, 0 = questionable)  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
C1: Clear exogenous timing (shock unforeseen) ………………… 1  
C2: Parallel pre-trends (will test and expect to hold) ………… 1  
C3: No simultaneous confounders differentially hitting groups … 0.5  
C4: No spillovers / interference (SUTVA) ………………………… 0.5  
C5: Correct functional form & standard errors ………………… 1  
TOTAL = 4 / 5  

================================================================  
The plan leverages an exogenous, well-timed shock and rich security-level data to identify how funding distress at prime funds transmits to otherwise unrelated corporate borrowers.
